comparison: Perfect agreement on VTNg lesion specificity and histological characterization (C29-C39). Both evaluations find the evidence for selective and complete lesions with minimal collateral damage to be well-supported. Reviewers describe lesions as 'very precise' while OpenEval notes 'strong support for lesion specificity.'

Disagreement on PCFx morphometric evidence (C40-C55). OpenEval finds the quantitative evidence supported despite acknowledged limitations in stereology. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, stating 'it is difficult to determine this from Figure 1G,H' and request improved photomicrographs and additional measurements, indicating the anatomical characterization is incomplete.

Agreement on T-maze behavioral findings (C58-C79). Both evaluations accept the behavioral results showing MTTx/VTNx impairments with appropriate statistical analyses. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'interesting and important results' and 'remarkable,' particularly the maze rotation effects. OpenEval notes coherent pattern with progressive cue restriction providing mechanistic insight.

Agreement on radial-arm maze results (C80-C94). Both evaluations support the convergence with T-maze findings showing consistent MTTx/VTNx impairments. Peer reviewers accept the behavioral dissociation between PCFx (no effect) and MTTx/VTNx lesions as a key finding. OpenEval emphasizes the maze rotation manipulation effectively tests allocentric versus intra-maze cue reliance.

Agreement on geometric discrimination task sparing (C95-C104). Both evaluations accept the intact performance in MTTx/VTNx groups. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as consistent with selectivity of spatial memory deficits. OpenEval emphasizes this dissociation as important evidence against non-specific factors and supports parallel memory systems within mammillary bodies (C176-C180).

Partial disagreement on retrosplenial cortex c-Fos findings (C107-C111). OpenEval finds clear evidence for differential effects with appropriate methodology. Peer reviewers acknowledge findings but express uncertainty, noting 'the situation is likely to be rather complicated and other pathways could also be directly or indirectly involved,' indicating concerns about interpretation complexity.

Disagreement on hippocampal c-Fos findings (C112-C119). OpenEval supports the CA1-specific reduction despite marginal p-value and acknowledges non-stereological limitations. Peer reviewers request more detailed analysis, specifically asking 'which neurons and layer are or are not c-Fos positive,' indicating the evidence is incomplete or insufficiently characterized.

Partial disagreement on prefrontal cortex c-Fos findings (C120-C123). OpenEval supports the prelimbic/infralimbic dissociation as evidence of anatomical specificity. Peer reviewers acknowledge findings but express general concern about c-Fos interpretation complexity and request more detailed characterization across brain regions.

Partial agreement on negative control c-Fos findings (C124-C127). OpenEval emphasizes these as important evidence for specificity, particularly lack of supramammillary/septal changes. Peer reviewers implicitly acknowledge these findings but their request for more detailed c-Fos analysis suggests they want additional characterization to strengthen conclusions.

Agreement on main conclusion about VTNg versus hippocampal inputs (C3-C7, C140-C145, C165, C188). Both evaluations support the overarching finding that VTNg inputs are more critical than hippocampal inputs for spatial memory. Peer reviewers describe the behavioral dissociation as 'interesting and important.' OpenEval notes converging evidence while acknowledging alternative explanations remain.

Agreement on need for better explanation of PCFx results (C154-C164, C156-C159, C187). Both evaluations recognize the surprising lack of PCFx effects requires interpretation. Peer reviewers explicitly request 'more detailed, explicit discussion' and ask 'What then is the role of the PCF?' OpenEval finds the discussion appropriately speculative but acknowledges tasks may not optimally test the hippocampal-MB pathway.

OpenEval evaluates historical context and theoretical framing (C1-C2, C8-C14, C128-C131) as supported, characterizing the literature review as accurate and appropriately motivating the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background material.

OpenEval evaluates anatomical background on medial/lateral mammillary systems (C15-C21, C132-C139) as well-supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this anatomical context.

OpenEval evaluates discussion of VTNx mechanisms and alternative pathways (C166-C175) as supported, noting c-Fos evidence from supramammillary/septal nuclei helps rule out alternatives. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers' general concern about pathway complexity may relate to these claims.

Agreement on interpretation of geometric discrimination dissociation (C176-C180). OpenEval supports the inference about task-specific neural systems and parallel memory pathways. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this interpretation as consistent with the overall pattern, treating the dissociation as evidence for selectivity.

OpenEval evaluates translational relevance discussion (C181-C186) as appropriately cautious about human VTNg evidence while noting cross-species conservation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this translational discussion.

Partial disagreement on synthesis of c-Fos findings (C147-C153). OpenEval finds the synthesis appropriate with measured interpretation of causal versus symptomatic relationships. Peer reviewers' request for more detailed c-Fos analysis and concern about pathway complexity suggests they find the synthesis incomplete or requiring additional support.
